{{Quote|The Republic Senate will pay for their crimes against the Gossam, their devastation of our economy, their condescension.|[[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]]|<ref name="Kinect Star Wars">''[[Kinect Star Wars]]''</ref>}}
'''Gossams''' were a small [[Reptile/Legends|saurian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Castell/Legends|Castell]] in the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], with colonies on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] worlds of [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] and [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]]. Averaging slightly over one [[Meter/Legends|meter]] in height, Gossams had wrinkled skin, with narrowing, shriveled heads on elongated necks. Physical appearance was considered important in Gossam society, and [[Gender/Legends|females]] often curved their hair up from the back of their heads. They were bipeds, balancing their frail bodies on small [[Limb/Legends|feet]], and had long three-fingered hands. The average lifespan of a Gossam was about seventy-five [[Standard year/Legends|years]].

Known for their shrewd and cunning nature, most Gossam on Castell served the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], which was headed by the Gossam [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]] and the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Due to their intelligent and scheming nature, Gossams could be found all over the galaxy, acting as either legitimate merchants or as law-breaking [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], while [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-using Gossam were extremely rare.

==Biology and appearance==
[[File:Gossam_NEGAS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A blue-skinned Gossam wearing an ornate hat]]
Gossam stood roughly 1.25 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] high, had pebbly green or blue skin, elongated necks, wide yellow [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and a tapered head that sloped back on an incline.<ref name="UAA" /> Gossam balanced their thin bodies on two three-toed feet, and had long, graceful three fingered hands.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Gossams developed at a reasonably standard rate. Considered [[Youngling/Legends|younglings]] until around the age of ten, society regarded them as full adults by the age of fourteen. Gossam reaching around sixty standard years were considered old, while those living past the age of seventy-five were considered venerable.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
Like most [[Reptile/Legends|reptiles]], Gossam young were hatched from [[Egg/Legends|eggs]]. Gossam mothers watched over the eggs more for the status than for any practical purpose. Because the species was so appearance driven, Gossam families would build nests of elegant warm fabrics and cushions to show off their young before they were even hatched. They would also throw egg parties where the eager parents would receive gifts from their friends and relatives. The higher the status of the parents, the larger the gifts. The parties were thrown late in the eggs' incubation period in the hope that the egg would hatch during the event.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:GossamUAA.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A Gossam]]
Gossams held their appearances as extremely important, and dressed in elaborate clothing in an attempt to impress other [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]]. [[Gender/Legends|Females]] used oil-based creams to mold their hair into a wave that traditionally swept up from the back of their heads.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Wealthy Gossam aristocrats and trade negotiators often wore elevated footwear to appear taller when dealing with other [[Species/Legends|species]], in addition to the exotic robes and finery favored by most Gossam.<ref name="UAA" />

Most Gossam were selfish, scheming beings skilled at the art of business.<ref name="UAA" /> Though most Gossam were intelligent and independently minded, many spent much of their lives working for the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]], who offered them food, housing and a decent income for a ten year exclusive contract.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Gossam goods were generally cheap to manufacture, and overpriced. Always looking for an angle they can play to come out on top, Gossam were considered untrustworthy by other beings.<ref name="UAA" />

The Gossam had a military in the form of [[Gossam Commandos/Legends|Gossam Commandos]], a group of male Gossam soldiers who wore heavy armor and used heavy [[Repeating blaster/Legends|repeating blasters]]. They also used a heavy shoulder-mounted cannon that took two Gossams to operate&mdash;one to fire and one to reload. Commerce Guild Presidente [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] personally authorized their use in the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="Reversal of Fortune">''[[Reversal of Fortune]]''</ref>

Gossam spoke a [[Gossam (language)/Legends|language]] of the same name. It consisted of lispy vocalizations, croaks and trills. Written Gossam had a jagged alphabet that combined into short words and long sentences.<ref name="UAA" /> Due to their industrial relationships with many offworld companies, most Gossam also spoke [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]].<ref name="NEGAS" />

Gossam names were usually quite short&mdash;both first names and surnames usually only had three or four letters. Common Gossam names were Min Cho, Xiri Gan, Zim Li, Shan Sien, and Mei Tran.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
[[File:Gossamcommando.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A [[Gossam Commandos/Legends|Gossam Commando]]]]
Circa [[27,000 BBY/Legends|27,000 BBY]], the Gossam experimented and developed the [[Tumbledrive/Legends|tumble hyperdrive]] which allowed them to colonize several distant worlds including [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] . Due to the aggressive plants and animals on that world, colonization was limited and the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] was used as a resort for wealthy Gossam and their servants.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

The Gossam executives managing a corporation called [[Subtext Mining]] were responsible for supplying [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]]("Rugess Nome") with an [[M-2 mining probe droid]] to examine a [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] deposit located on [[Bal'demnic/Legends|Bal'demnic]] in [[67 BBY/Legends|67 BBY]]. The probe droid, on detecting a pocket of gas ignored the shutdown command and kept drilling resulting in an explosion that [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]]("Hego Damask") exploited and used to kill his master Tenebrous. Damask, on returning to his homeworld of [[Muunilinst/Legends|Muunilinst]] instructs [[Larsh Hill]] to invite the owners of Subtext Mining to the upcoming [[Gathering (Sojourn)|Gathering]] on Sojourn. He confronted the Gossam executives representing Subtext Mining who, in a panic, blurted out information related to a survey job which had revealed a massive untapped [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] reservoir buried beneath [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] on the Mid Rim planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] to save their lives. Damask spared them temporarily and ordered the [[Sun Guard]] to exile the four Gossam executives to the most remote world on the [[Tingel Arm/Legends|Tingel Arm]] to be held indefinitely till he has further use for them. Two years later on [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] in [[65 BBY/Legends|65 BBY]], Damask, on learning that Subtext Mining had approached [[Gran Protectorate/Legends|Gran Protectorate]] Senator [[Pax Teem]] because of the disappearance of the exiled Gossam executives, ordered Larsh Hill to have the Sun Guard execute them and dump their bodies at [[Subtext Mining Corporate Headquarters|Subtext Mining's corporate headquarters]] on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]].<ref>[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']] {{Ab|Darth Plagueis (audiobook)}}</ref>

For ten years before the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], the Gossam homeworld of [[Castell/Legends|Castell]] suffered a devastating economic depression due to the heavy taxation of trade routes. This resulted in a loss of profits and little demand for goods from Castell. Many Gossam resorted to fighting over food, jobs and passage offworld, until the Commerce Guild appointed Shu Mai as its president. Mai almost single-handedly helped Castell out of this depression due to her aggressive business practices, her support of the Gossam workforce, and her taciturn negotiation tactics.<ref name="UAA" /> Mai had each able Gossam serve as an indentured servant of the Commerce Guild for a portion of their lives. In return, they were offered food, housing and a modest income. Most Gossam saw this as the dreary reality. Once Castell grew out of its economic depression, this tradition continued, with most young Gossams taking indentured contracts to gain business experience before venturing out into the corporate world alone. Many Gossam made large profits by investing their credits in offworld bank accounts, not trusting their own people. Still others built offworld estates on [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]] and Felucia, thus starting Gossam colonies on those [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] worlds.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:Shu_Sullust.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Gossam on [[Bassadro]]]]
Just before the outbreak of the Clone Wars, Shu Mai secretly pledged her support to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], despite realizing that it would amount to [[Treason/Legends|treason]]. Her reasons were simple&mdash;she couldn't resist a potentially profitable venture.<ref name="ShuDB">{{DB|character|shumai|Mai, Shu}}</ref> The Commerce Guild pledged massive amounts of [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|DSD1 dwarf spider droids]], as well as the Gossam Commandos.<ref name="ComDB">{{DB|organization|ca_tankdroid|Commerce Guild}}</ref> The Gossam as a species did not pledge their support to the CIS, but as they were considered the property of the Commerce Guild, they were expected to help the war effort whenever possible. Due to this, during the Clone Wars, Gossam were banished from Coruscant.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Amita Fonti/Legends|Amita Fonti]], a Gossam [[Senator/Legends|senator]], attended a convening of the [[Separatist Senate/Legends|Separatist Parliament]] on the planet [[Raxus Secundus|Raxus]], where she supported a motion to open [[Confederate–Republic peace initiative/Legends|peace negotiations]] with the Republic.<ref name="HOBS">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref>

In the months after the Clone Wars, many Gossam on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] joined [[Whiplash]], a resistance movement working against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="sos">''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]''</ref> The Gossam were ultimately enslaved by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and very few were able to join the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] after its formation. Due to their former alliance with the CIS, the Gossam and their [[Planet/Legends|planet]] were a primary target of [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] reign of terror against [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] species. The species was even banned from setting foot on Coruscant, a law enacted without warning to the many Gossam merchants, pilots, and travelers already present. Enforcement began at once: their ships and assets were seized, and many were arrested. Some, however, escaped capture through underworld ties, shipping guilds, or simple cunning, while a few managed to flee offworld. Most remained stranded on Coruscant as wanted criminals. Not until after the Alliance's victory did they receive their freedom; however, Castell still had not fully recovered as of the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].<ref name="Desperate Allies">''[[Desperate Allies]]''</ref><ref name="NEGAS" />

After the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], several Gossam worked for the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. It was unclear whether the Gossam joined the [[Confederation]] after the [[Corporate Sector Authority/Legends|Corporate Sector Authority]] allied itself with the Confederation. However, this was unlikely because several were seen working for the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] with a supply company.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref>

==Gossam in the galaxy==
[[File:Coru_gossam.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A Gossam on the planet Coruscant in 22 BBY]]
Many Gossam established offworld estates for recreational purposes, on planets like Felucia and Saleucami. Gossam were well known as some of the shrewdest business people in the known [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Their products were nearly always inexpensive to manufacture in mass, and extremely overpriced. Gossam were excellent barterers, although their self-centered and greedy nature often led them to cheating and lying to amass as many credits as possible. A Gossam's word was rarely valued, both by Gossam and those with whom they were doing business. Some members of the species were legitimate merchants&mdash;although most were quite the opposite.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Large numbers of Gossam were involved with piracy and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] operations. Due to their size and calm demeanor, Gossam were frequently underestimated&mdash;a perception they were happy to exploit.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Most [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] [[Captain/Legends|captains]] paid little heed to reports of Gossam piracy- until blaster--wielding Gossam raided their ships.<ref name="UAA" /> However, Gossam rarely rose to positions of power, with Shu Mai being one of very few exceptions. This was largely due to the fact that their innate independence and lust for profits seems to prohibit the long-term planning needed to achieve real influence.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Gossam were extremely rare,<ref name="UAA" /> though at least one Gossam was [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|initiated]] in the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] as part of the [[Soaring Hawkbat Clan]] studying at a [[Bogden Jedi chapter house|training facility]] on [[Bogden 3]] at the end of the Clone Wars in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Dark Times 6">[[Dark Times 6|''Dark Times'' 6]]</ref> Those Gossam who were not [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] or merchants often worked as tech-specialists.<ref name="UAA" /> One group of Gossam worked as bussers at the [[Corusca Gem casino]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] during the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]].<ref name="PID">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030417positiveid|text=Positive ID|int=Positive ID}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Gossam species were created for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], and first appeared in ''[[The Approaching Storm]]'', by [[Alan Dean Foster]]. In both ''Attack of the Clones'' and [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], Shu Mai and the other Gossam characters are entirely computer-generated.<ref name="ShuDB" /> The history and culture of the species has since been expanded upon by numerous sources.
